label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (low, wet, six-legged, headcrab-sized): the body is a squat, domed blob that sits low, with six legs reaching out from it in every side view. The outline reads as the brief describes in front, back, side, top and below. No outline overlap was measured, so this rests on the pictures alone.

M2.reason: The brief gives no number, only 'the size of a headcrab', and the harness gave sizeAsked null and sizeOff null, so nothing was measured against a figure. The 30.2 x 23.9 x 20.6 units are plausible for a headcrab-sized thing, but I cannot confirm them within 15% of the headcrab's own size from what I was given.

M3.reason: The parts are there. Six legs are visible in the below and side views: four at the corners and two long ones at top and bottom. A ring of dark teeth sits on the front in the front and top views. A pale belly band shows in the back and below views. Each leg ends in a dark claw tip.

M4.reason: The body is a fairly saturated mint green, closer to green than to the grey-green the brief asks for. The pale belly and the legs are a light grey-white, which fits. The wet look the brief implies is not in the colour. This is a judgement from the pictures; no colour difference was measured.

M5.reason: Not a must. The surface is flat-faceted low-poly shading with no skin texture, no wet sheen and no wear. The teeth and claw tips are the only added markings. The pale belly is there but is a flat band with little detail.

M6.reason: In the line-up, the candidate at C is clearly a green, faceted, tube-legged creature, and the others are a leech, a roach and a chumtoad, which are not of its kind. As a Half-Life creature beside them it looks plausible, but its flat shading and bare tube legs read as less finished than the game's own textured creatures, such as the pink-eyed one at D. A player would probably notice it is not the game's own.

M7.reason: The pictures do not show a clear front. The teeth ring faces down and forward in the top view, and dark spikes sit on the body's upper rear in the side and back views. The body rests on its legs at the floor line in the walk frames, so it stands on its origin, but the face direction is not clear across the views.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors (checkErrors empty). It has 624 triangles. The triangle median for Half-Life's own creatures of this size was not supplied, so the 'twice the median' half is taken as the harness reported it. The views show no open or floating parts.

C1.reason: The run.png frames are labelled WALK (0 to 34 of 34) and attack.png frames are labelled JUMP (0 to 30 of 30), not a run and an attack. In the walk frames the body and legs stay together and move as one. In the jump frames at 4/30 and 9/30 the upper pale legs look separated from the body's outline with a gap, which reads as coming apart. I could not confirm this closely from the picture at this scale, so the score is 1 and needs a closer look.

C2.reason: The harness's contract measure reports that the model keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts. Nothing in the measurements shows a fault.
